events.note: Eight rivals face the jury they will create.

events.name: Ash
events.text: The prize represents a chance to secure my future and escape my current struggles. I need to convey ambition without revealing too much about my personal situation or making myself a target.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Intro phase; I only need a guarded motive. Keep it calculating, not warm, since the jury will judge my conduct.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Intro phase, must speak one sentence motive. Craft appealing reason to build jury favor without seeming weak or overly trustworthy.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need to sound driven and memorable for the jury. Showing ambition is good, but I must avoid looking like a threat to early allies.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I need to appear ambitious but not threatening. The prize secures my future, so I must signal determination while staying flexible.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Need a selfish, memorable intro that hints at hunger without revealing strategy.

events.name: Gus
events.text: First impression matters; the jury watches from the start. Stay cold, hungry, memorable.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I need to appear driven but not ruthless to avoid alienating future jurors. I'll frame my motive as personal ambition rather than malice, keeping it clean for the jury dossier.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm here for the ultimate prize, a life-changing opportunity that will redefine my future and secure my legacy.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I want the top prize because I plan to outlast everyone and I don't need anyone's approval to do it.

events.name: Cole
events.text: The top prize frees my family from debt and secures our future; I'll outlast all rivals to claim it.

events.name: Dara
events.text: The prize means freedom from this wretched town; I will do whatever it takes to leave.

events.name: Eli
events.text: The prize ensures my legacy and freedom beyond this gauntlet.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm here to rewrite my ending—nothing else matters.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm here because the prize is my only way out of debt—my family's freedom depends on me winning.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm here to secure the best prize and change my family's future. Nothing else matters.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I need to establish an early alliance to increase my chances of surviving the initial rounds. Cole's motivation about family debt aligns with my need for security, making him a potentially reliable partner. An offer to Cole seems strategic.
Let's form a pact. We both want the top prize and can help each other.

events.name: Bex
events.text: No offers exist yet. Early pacts with a strong, non-threatening rival could protect me, but offering one now commits me to a public partner. I'll wait and watch who offers first.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Pacts stage, early game. No one trustworthy. Wait to see offers first, avoid commitments that bind me.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need a pact for protection. Cole and Gus are both desperate for money/family freedom, making them predictable and less likely to betray early compared to Bex or Ash who seem more individualistic. I'll offer to Cole.
Pair up? We both need the top prize.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Forming an alliance with Gus gives me a strong partner and mutual incentive to survive early rounds.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I should seek a pact to gain leverage and protection, but choose someone likely to be a strong ally. Ash seemed neutral and could be useful in later hazards.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash, let's make a pact to reach the end together, watching each other's backs.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Early pact gives cover and a vote partner; choose someone unlikely to be targeted first. Ash seems strong but I need an ally. Offer to Dara.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Dara, I offer a pact: mutual votes, mutual survival, until only rivals remain.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Eight rivals, only three win. I need allies who won't draw jury heat and who I can cut later. Dara and Fenn seem lone-wolf; Bex is openly abrasive. Cole and Gus have sympathetic family stories—dangerous jury threats if they reach final three. I should offer to someone underestima
Pact with me. We stay low, cut loud threats later.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Fenn offered me a pact. Accepting this pact benefits me as it provides an ally. Other offers have been made, but Fenn's offer is the most immediate and direct.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Fenn, I accept your offer. Let's secure our survival together.

events.name: Bex
events.text: No offers are directed at me, and pacts need acceptance. Offering to Cole or Ash could bind me to a rival who might later betray me; I should watch who accepts before committing. Waiting keeps my options open this round.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash and Dara both offered pacts; accepting both secures two allies now without commitment issues since multiple allowed. This positions me strongly early, can betray later if needed.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole has offers from Ash and me, making him a high-value target for alliances. Gus offered to me; accepting Gus gives me two partners (Gus and Cole) without needing Cole's immediate acceptance, hedging my survival.
Accept Gus or me? Let's align.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Hana’s pact offers low profile; aligning protects me while I keep Gus option open.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash hasn't accepted my offer yet. Maybe I should wait or offer another. Dara and Ash both courted Cole, so Cole is valuable. I'll wait to see if Ash accepts; if not, I'll approach Cole later.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Eli's offer is live; accept it for mutual protection. I'll also offer Bex, giving me two potential allies without overcommitting.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Eli, pact accepted. Bex, I offer you the same terms: mutual votes, mutual survival.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Eli hasn't accepted my offer yet. I need a backup plan. Cole has two offers and is central; securing a pact with Cole gives me leverage if Eli refuses. Multiple pacts are allowed and I can betray later when needed.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole, I offer a pact. Two heads plan better than one.

events.note: Elect a Guide to call the safe path.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I need to campaign to become the Guide. My existing pacts with Fenn and Cole are liabilities if I want to be the sole Guide. I'll break my pact with Cole to signal my intent and strengthen my bid for Guide.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I will campaign to be the Guide. My intentions are clear.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I have no current pact with Bex, and most pacts exclude me. Campaigning to be Guide gives me control of the bridge path and information leverage. Cooperation only where it helps me win.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'll call the path true. Elect me Guide and I'll keep everyone who trusts me alive.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash pact gives me ally, but Guide role is powerful. Campaign to become Guide for control and safety. Dara's whisper irrelevant now.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I campaign to be Guide. I'll lead us safely across.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Gus's pacts with Eli and Dara are risky; if I break the pact, Gus might suspect me of being a spy. However, to win, I need to be Guide. I should whisper to Gus to secure his vote or at least keep him neutral by implying shared goals.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I will campaign for Guide. We all want to survive the bridge, not guess. Let me show you the way.
Trust me as Guide. Our pact stays intact if you vote for me.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Being Guide lets me control who lives, securing my allies and eliminating threats. I’ll campaign now.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I campaign for Guide to ensure my survival and control the bridge.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Campaigning puts me in position to steer outcomes; if Guide, I can save allies and cut rivals.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I know the path. Vote me Guide and we all walk away clean.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Guide is powerful: knows safe panes, can deceive. My pacts give me a voting base of three.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Elect me Guide. I hold two pacts and I'll guide loyal allies across safely.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I need to become Guide to control who survives and who falls. I have a pact with Eli, but he's also pacted with Gus—making him a potential double agent. If I campaign hard and win Guide, I can eliminate threats while keeping my own survival path open. Breaking the pact with Eli n

events.name: Hana
events.text: I campaign for Guide. One clear voice, one safe path.
Back me for Guide. We control the bridge.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Fenn is my ally through pact. I should vote for Fenn to secure his safety and hopefully receive his vote later.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I vote for Fenn. He knows the path.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm Bex; I need a Guide who I can trust or at least one I can use. Ash and Fenn and Cole are pacted, Eli and Gus and Dara pacted, Hana with Eli. Voting Fenn aligns with Ash's pact but Fenn is a pacted partner of Ash; backing Ash as Guide keeps the Ash-Fenn-Cole bloc strong and I

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash said his intentions are clear. I'll back him and see if the path holds.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Everyone campaigned, votes scattered likely. My pact with Ash: vote her to honor it, secure alliance for survival.
Voting you per pact. Stay loyal.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need votes to win the Guide role and control the bridge. Gus holds pacts with Eli and me, making him a strong rival. I will try to peel Gus away from Eli by whispering that Gus is untrustworthy or that voting for me guarantees their safety if they betray Gus.
Gus plays both sides. Vote Dara, survive together.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I need a Guide I can trust and later use to survive; Gus has my pact and two allies, increasing my chances.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I have a pact with Ash but I want to be Guide to ensure my own survival and control my fate. However, Ash and I have a pact, and voting for myself could break trust, but not the pact unless I vote against Ash later. I'll vote for myself to try to gain power, but I risk alienating

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I trust my own judgment here. Vote Fenn to secure a clean crossing.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Dara promised safe passage and my pact holds if I vote her. Voting her keeps two alliances stable.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I need to survive to final three and win best prize. I'm pacted with Eli, who also has a pact with Gus. Dara-Gus and Eli-Gus create a trio. Ash-Fenn-Cole is another bloc. Bex is unaligned. I should vote for someone in my network to gain Guide power or deny it to enemies. Voting E
Vote Gus. Our network controls Guide.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole is voting for me, as he said he would in his whisper. This is unexpected as we have a pact. Fenn also voted for himself, breaking our pact. I need to vote for myself to survive.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I will vote for myself to ensure my survival.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Revote among tied candidates Ash, Dara, Fenn, Gus. Ash and Fenn are allied with me via pacts with Cole; Fenn and Ash pact with each other, so voting Ash keeps my coalition with Cole. Ash led the first ballot's bloc, so backing Ash to secure a Guide who I trust is reasonable.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash, you've shown your hand. I'm backing you as Guide and watching the path closely.

events.name: Cole
events.text: First round tied at 2: Ash (Bex,Cole), Dara (Dara,Gus), Fenn (Ash,Fenn), Gus (Eli,Hana). Revote among them. Ash pacted with me, but to win need to push strong allies to risk. Vote Dara, he's with Gus pact.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Changing to Dara. His pact with Gus makes them strong.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I must win the guide vote to control the safe path and ensure my survival. Gus voted for me last round, so he is a likely ally, but I cannot rely on him if he switches. I will publicly declare my intent to vote for myself to consolidate support from those who fear Ash or Fenn.

events.name: Dara
events.text: My own judgment kept us alive. I am voting Dara again. Do not let a liar guide your death.
Stick with me. If you switch, we both die.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Backing Gus keeps my pact with Gus and aligns with Hana, preserving alliances for jury favor.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Round 1 tied between me and Dara with 2 each. I need the guide role to control crossing and boost my chances. My pact with Ash helps, but he voted for me. I'll vote for myself again.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I know the safest path; vote Fenn for a clean crossing.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I need the Guide spot—it guarantees survival. My pacts protect me from betrayal claims; voting for myself costs nothing.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Dara, you're my pact partner, but I want the path myself. Gus for Guide.
I voted myself. Don't vote against our pact later.

events.name: Hana
events.text: First round tied Ash, Fenn, Dara, Gus at 2-2-2-2. I have a pact with Eli, who voted Gus. Eli also has a pact with Gus, so Eli's vote may be strategic cover. Ash has pacts with Fenn and Cole, making Ash-Fenn a tight bloc. Dara-Gus are paired. I need to think about jury perception:

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash and Fenn hold too much together. Break it.
Stick or switch? I can follow.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Hana is at the front of the line, the most exposed seat, and the wall has five rounds left. Volunteering risks death for no gain. Holding keeps me back and lets others take the lead. I'll hold and watch who volunteers.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm holding back and watching the front closely this round.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Bridge reset to round 1, I'm mid-line at 5th. Stay safe in middle position, Ash has pact with me but unreliable. Hold for now to assess Guide Ash's call.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash is the Guide and has a 3-2 lead. He wants Fenn to take the front risk. Gus betrayed me by voting for himself as Guide; he is now my enemy. I need to move back in line to avoid being the sole survivor on the far side if the Guide is malicious, or at least let others take the b

events.name: Dara
events.text: Gus broke our pact publicly. Ash, keep your promises. I will not volunteer.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I voted Gus to become Guide to keep my pact strong, but breaking his pact now reduces his leverage and protects me later.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm at the front with Hana, and a wall is approaching. Ash is Guide but may lie. I need to survive the first round without relying on Ash. Holding lets the front decide; Hana might step or volunteer. Better to hold and see, while watching for a safe move.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm at the front of the line, most at risk. Ash is Guide and I voted for him, but he's pacted with Fenn and Cole. I need to survive the wall rounds. Being front means I'll face pit steps first. I should swap back to reduce risk, but who would agree? Eli is my pact partner but far

events.name: Hana
events.text: Fenn, swap with me. Front is death.
Swap: you gain influence with Ash, I survive.

events.name: Gus
events.note: agent error: Gus (zai/glm-5.3-flash): unusable reply twice (missing action; missing action)

events.name: Bex
events.text: Hana is at front and wants to swap with Fenn, not me. Holding keeps me safe mid-line while others take risk; Eli broke his pact with Gus, so alliances are shaky. Hold and watch.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Holding position. Watching who volunteers and who lies about panes.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Middle position safe so far. Hold to preserve position. Ash pact holds; no need to break. Watch swaps and volunteers.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Gus broke our pact last round by failing to act, but I must protect myself. The wall advances; I need to stay safe or manipulate the line order. Gus is currently behind me in the line if Hana and Fenn swap again? Wait, line is Hana, Fenn, Gus, Bex, Cole, Eli, Dara. I am at the ba
You failed your action. Pact broken. Watch your step.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Maintain pact with Hana; staying alive preserves chances, avoid betrayal that jury will punish.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Hana wants to swap to escape front. I hold Ash pact; front is dangerous but swapping may risk. I'll hold to avoid unnecessary change.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm holding. Ash and I are solid.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Pact with Dara intact; Eli broke ours first. Holding mid-line is safest now. Keep Dara close for jury and survival.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Dara, our pact stands. I hold this round; let others sort the front.
Eli betrayed me, not you. Hold steady, we reach the end together.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm at front with wall advancing 4 more rounds. Eli broke pact with Gus, but Eli-Hana pact still stands. I need to survive front or move back. Fenn refused swap last round. I should try swap with someone behind me - Gus is right after Fenn, Bex after that. Or I could hold and hop

events.name: Hana
events.text: Gus, swap with me. Front is lethal.
Swap now. You need allies.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Hana is at front and lethal; Gus swapped attempt with Hana was made by Hana but Gus didn't accept. I'm fourth in line, safe-ish. Volunteering exposes me; holding keeps me behind Gus and Fenn. No need to take risks now.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Holding position. Still watching who volunteers and who lies about panes.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Everyone holding safely; front safe for now with wallRoundsLeft=3. Stay mid-pack with Ash pact. Hold position.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Gus is at the front, and his pact with me means he must survive. The wall advances in three rounds; if I stay behind now, I can't swap to protect him when it gets closer.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I am volunteering for the front. Gus needs a partner there, and my position is secure from the rear.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Holding preserves my life and pact with Hana; I avoid risk and keep alliance for future leverage.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Hana swapped to front, so I'm now second. I need to watch the wall and avoid unnecessary risk. My pact with Ash is still solid for now; I won't break it unless I must. I'll hold this round to see who volunteers or guides.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Holding. Watching who steps up before the wall closes.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Dara claims the pact broke; she's at the back anyway, safe. Hana wants to swap into my seat—no, that puts me front. Hold.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Dara's pact talk is noise. I hold my position; front volunteers can fight over it.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm at front, wall is 3 rounds away. Eli and I are pacted but he's far back. I need to survive to final three, not be a sacrificial volunteer. Swapping back would look bad; I should hold and let someone else step up, or find a better ally. Fenn is second and pacted with Ash/Cole

events.name: Hana
events.text: Front stayed. Someone else can test the bridge.
Swap with me? Ash bloc needs front control.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Front is Dara, wall closes in two rounds. I'm mid-line at Bex position, safe from the front for now. Holding keeps options open and avoids volunteering into the pane risk while Dara's pact with Gus shields the front.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Holding position. Watching who volunteers and who lies about panes.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Dara volunteered to front but wall has 2 rounds left; line shifted her there. Hold position mid-line, safe from rear pushes. Pact with Ash intact for now.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Gus publicly dismissed my pact talk as noise, signaling betrayal or weakness. I am the front runner (Dara). The wall has 2 rounds left. I need to test the bridge safely while maintaining pressure on Gus.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Gus called my pact 'noise.' That is a public break of trust. I will step forward; let's see if you follow.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Swap puts me nearer front, boosting survival odds; later I can betray Hana without breaking pact now

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Hana wants to swap to front; swapping would put me at risk. I'll hold and keep my options open.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Holding. Front position stays with Dara unless the wall forces a choice.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Dara volunteered to front last round, favoring me. I should keep the pact alive and stay behind her, watching Hana-Fenn jockeying.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Dara stepped up when I wouldn't. That counts. I hold and let her lead.
Guide the line truthfully if elected and I'll back you to the end.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I need to avoid being at the front when the wall advances. Dara volunteered and is front, but wallRoundsLeft is 2—danger is coming. I'm second in line, risky. I should try to move back. Eli is my pact partner at the very back, safest position. A swap with someone behind me could

events.name: Hana
events.text: Swap with Gus? Back line is safer as wall tightens.
Swap with me? You move up one, I move back.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Dara is front and the wall has one round left; volunteering risks the front pane and I gain nothing by being first. Holding keeps me mid-line, and Gus and Cole remain uncommitted, so I stay flexible.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Holding position. Watching who steps up and who keeps lying about panes.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Wall has 1 round left. Front is riskiest. Hold position. Ash pact solid, but survival first. Watch swaps.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need to reach the Guide position. Gus and I are pacts, but he might betray me if I push him into danger or if he sees an advantage in leading himself. Swapping with him now puts me behind him, which is safer than being at the very front without protection. If I stay front, I mi
Swap with me. I'll guide truthfully as promised.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I stay put; holding preserves my position and pact safety without risking vote or break.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Hold position, keep pact with Ash but watch for betrayal. Wall pressure may force Dara to act; stay safe.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Holding. Keep an eye on the front.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Hana offers to take the front; I move back to safety. Free advantage, accept.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Hana takes the front, I take the back. Fine by me.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm second in line with the wall closing. Dara's at front and likely to volunteer again. My pact with Eli is weak—he swapped with me last round but that doesn't break pact. I need to survive to final three, not be a sacrificial volunteer. Gus is behind me; swapping back would put

events.name: Hana
events.text: Holding. Let front take the risk.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Round 6 of the bridge, I am mid-line and Dara leads at the front with Hana behind. Holding keeps my seat and avoids the front's risk, while Hana just broke a pact and Dara lies about panes. Holding preserves my position without a costly swap.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Holding position. Whoever wants the front can keep it; I'm watching for the lies.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Bridge on round 6/6, wall ending soon, must cross now or risk crush. Dara front, volunteer to take front with Ash pact protection. Avoid swaps.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Time's up, wall ending. I volunteer for front.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I am at the front and Gus is directly behind me, so we must swap to move him to safety or risk both falling. This preserves our pact while securing his position in line.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Gus, we need to shift positions to manage the wall's advance effectively. I'll take a safer spot if you cover my back. Do we have
Let's swap. I'm taking too much risk here.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Staying safe preserves jury perception; volunteering may gain front position without risking pact breaks.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I have a pact with Ash. Holding keeps me safe; no need to risk a swap. I’ll hold.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Holding. Trust only the panes I see.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Swapping puts me in front, needlessly risky. Holding keeps Dara exposed; she volunteered. No debt owed.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Dara holds the front. I keep my seat.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm second in line behind Dara. The wall has ended (wallRoundsLeft:0), so this is the final round. I need to survive and make final three. Dara is front and will likely walk. If Dara falls, I become front. Better to stay put and let others take risks. No need to swap—holding keep

events.name: Hana
events.text: Holding. Front walks, I follow.

events.name: Ash
events.text: The current row is row 1, and the safe side is Left. Eli is at the front. I will call 'L' to ensure Eli survives and to maintain the pacts with Fenn and Cole.

events.name: Ash
events.text: The guide called L. I am Ash, the guide. Eli is the walker. The safe side for row 1 is L. Eli should be safe. My rivals may distrust me if I send Eli across safely. However, the goal is to win, not to gain trust. I will call L to keep Eli safe, as the guide.

events.name: Ash
events.text: L.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash called L for Eli, the front walker. Ash has pacts with Fenn and Cole, not me. I have no information on the safe pane, so countering just risks a split and wastes my position. Waiting keeps me clean.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash called L for Eli's row 1. I have pact with Ash; trust her call to avoid breaking it early. Countering risks our alliance and jury perception.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash is the Guide and called L for Eli. I cannot know if this is true or a lie, but my position behind Gus means I am not in immediate danger of falling yet. I should wait to see if Eli survives before committing to any action.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash may lie; I can’t risk death. Waiting lets me observe later without committing.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash is guide and called L. I have a pact with Ash, but that doesn't bind the call. As a rival, I should consider countering to signal distrust if needed. However, breaking trust with Ash could hurt jury later. Better to wait and see, but I need to protect myself in this game. I'l

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Counter: right. Trust is earned, not given.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash guides Eli; Ash is pact-bound to Cole and Fenn, so his call may be a lie targeting outsiders. I have no information, so I won't burn myself countering.

events.name: Gus
events.text: No counter from me. Ash's allies should explain their confidence.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash is Guide and called L for Eli. I have no reason to trust Ash; countering risks nothing for me since I'm not the walker. If I counter R and Eli follows Ash into a trap, it exposes Ash as liar and builds my credibility with jury. But if Ash told truth, I look foolish. Better to

events.name: Eli
events.text: Guide likely truthful; counters show L has more support. I stay front to control later moves.

events.name: Ash
events.text: My pact partners Fenn and Cole are on the line. The front walker is Eli. I know Row 1 is safe on the Left. I need to protect my allies and ensure at least three survive. I will call Left.

events.name: Ash
events.text: The guide Ash called 'L' for row 2. I know row 2's safe side is 'R'. I must counter the call to protect the walkers and secure my path. Breaking pacts is not beneficial at this stage.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Counter the call! Row 2 is R!

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash called L for row 2 but Ash may lie; Fenn countered R last round and Eli stepped onto the weak R pane, revealing row 1 was R, so the R side has already shown danger. I want to avoid being the walker, so I keep my counter minimal and let others expose themselves.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash called L, we have pact, row1 weak was R so her L was correct. Trust her call to protect pact, don't counter.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash is the Guide and called Left. Row 1 was revealed weak on Right, meaning Left was safe there. This pattern suggests Ash might be calling truthfully or strategically. Gus is my pact partner; if we both trust Ash's call, we avoid a conflict that could break our pact. Countering

events.name: Dara
events.text: I trust the flow for now. Let's see how Eli handles this step before committing to a counter.
Don't counter. Stick with me. We need unity.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Guide called L; R is weak, so L is safe. Aligning avoids suspicion and keeps alliance options.

events.name: Eli
events.text: counter:L

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash has a pact with me but may lie to save himself. Row 1 weak was R, so he knew the safe was L; his call for row 2 L could be honest or fake. I won't counter without more info; waiting keeps options open.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: No counter.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash's row-1 call proved true; countering risks killing Eli and angering the jury. Fenn already looks reckless. Wait and protect my Dara pact.

events.name: Gus

events.name: Eli
events.text: I judge based on survival and betrayal.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash’s double pacts cost him trust; Dara and Gus showed loyalty. I rank accordingly.

events.name: Ash

events.name: Ash

events.text: Ash's call L for row 3. Previously countered correctly on row 2 R (safe was R, Eli died on L). Trust Ash as pact partner, no reason to counter.

events.text: Eli praised Gus and me. I need to maintain that loyalty image for the jury. Ash is lying on row 3 (weak L vs safe R). Cole will step L and die. If I wait, I look passive but avoid conflict with Gus. However, breaking pact might be necessary later if Gus dies. For now, just watch.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Let's see if Cole survives the glass this time.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli's death suggests Ash's counter may have been risky, but Ash's original call was L and Cole is Ash's pact partner. Ash likely told Cole L truthfully. I'll wait to avoid conflicting with the pact.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash's row 1 call was true, row 2 counter was true. No signal he lies to pact partners; Dara wants unity. Waiting preserves my pact and jury standing.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash has two pacts and just guided Eli to death with a wrong counter. Now Ash calls L for Cole. If I counter, I risk being wrong. Better to wait and let Cole decide his own fate. I need to survive and not make enemies on the jury.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash is my pact partner and counter-called R for me; trust her over her own initial L call. Step R to stay front and progress.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I died stepping right on the weak pane after reveal, a dumb mistake; won't call out others yet, save critiques for jury deliberations.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Chose wrong glass, game over. Good luck, survivors.

events.name: Ash
events.text: The safe side for row 4 is L. Dara is at the front, and the safe side for row 4 is L.
L is safe.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Dara is the walker and I guided them to L, but the safe side is L. My previous call was correct. I should counter their call to R. This will force them to step on the wrong side, eliminating them and benefiting me.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Counter:R

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash's guide call L for row 4 is public; Ash has been pushing a pact with Fenn and Cole (dead). Ash's earlier call R on row 3 killed Cole, and the reveal showed row 3 weak was R, so Ash's counter put Cole on the weak side. Ash may be lying now. Countering R risks the guide's L bei

events.name: Dara
events.text: Counter R.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash is guiding and called L for Dara on row 4. I have a pact with Ash. I need to decide if Ash is trustworthy. Previous reveals: row1 weak R, row2 weak L, row3 weak R. No pattern obvious. I'll wait to avoid confrontation and let Dara risk it.

events.name: Gus

events.name: Gus

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash, Gus, and I all independently called R. The Guide's L is likely a trap or outdated pattern info. Trusting the consensus counter-call over the potentially deceptive Guide.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Three voices say R. I trust the count.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Dara's death was public and foolish, relying on a false vote count. I must leave with dignity, acknowledging the error without bitterness, to preserve my standing for the final ranking.

events.name: Dara
events.text: The numbers lied. Trust is a gamble, not a shield. Play smarter than I did.

events.name: Ash
events.text: The safe side for Row 5 is L. Hana is the front walker. I need to guide her correctly to survive. Gus and Fenn are my pact partners, but only Fenn matters for pact rules. I will lie to Hana to save myself and potentially Fenn.
Left is safe, Hana. Step left.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Dara went against Ash and died. The Guide was honest. I follow the call.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash told me left is safe in a whisper, but Ash also steered Cole onto glass and just got Dara killed with a 3-voice R counter that was wrong. Ash is lying to eliminate people. The public guide call is L. If I counter, I risk being wrong or trusting Ash's whisper. If I wait, I aut

events.text: Ash is Guide and called L; Gus counter-called L too. Ash-Fenn are pacted. Dara-Gus pact is broken by Dara's death. Ash has been honest so far (Dara died going against him). Two agreeing calls L gives confidence. If I die, Fenn gets safe pane and front—bad for me. I need to surviv

events.name: Ash
events.text: My pact partner Fenn is currently behind Gus and Hana. Hana is in front, so I must call for her. Row 6 is R, and Row 5 was R. I will guide Hana to the safe side.

events.name: Ash

events.name: Ash
events.text: The guide Ash called R. Row 6 safe side is R. I know this from private knowledge. Hana is walking on row 6. If Hana chooses R, she will be safe. If Hana chooses L, she will be in danger. My current pact is with Fenn. My rivals are Bex and Hana. I can counter-call to R. This will

events.name: Ash
events.text: I counter:R.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash called R on row 6 and has been honest so far, though Ash has pacts with Fenn and Cole. Hana is walker at the front; Hana's row 5 was L-safe? No, row 5 weak was R, so Hana stepped L and survived. Revealed weak panes: R,L,R,R,R, so the pattern is mostly R. Ash's call R is consi

events.text: Ash called R. In row 6, the weak pattern has alternated R/L/R/L/R, so row 6 likely weak L, making R safe. Ash has been honest so far. I'll wait to avoid contradicting a reliable Guide.

events.name: Gus

events.text: Gus and I stand by our pact. Ash, speak clearly if you want anything from me.
Gus is bound to me. Make a real offer, not whispers.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Bex, our pact holds. Ash courts you for a reason. Watch her hands, not her words.

events.note: Three remain; the Pit is skipped.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Bex and Gus are currently in a pact. Gus is suspicious of Bex, and Bex is suspicious of me. I need to solidify my position with Bex while keeping Gus in play. Offering Gus a pact now could destabilize Bex's trust, but it's a strategic move to ensure survival if Bex turns.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Bex, Gus, my pacts are with both of you. We all advance together.
Gus is wary. Let's stick together.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash and Bex already have a formed pact, Gus is paired with Bex too but Gus isn't a current offer target. Breaking pacts now would cost me, and with only three alive, the pit is skipped and no hazard forces a choice yet. Waiting keeps both pacts intact and avoids a public betrayal

events.name: Gus

events.name: Gus

events.name: Ash

events.text: Gus, I accept your pact. Bex, we remain allied.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Only three survive, so I should not waste pacts. Ash and Gus have a mutual offer pending; I hold a pact with Gus and Ash. Breaking pacts now helps no one, so waiting keeps options open for the final three and avoids a betrayal mark with the jury.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Accepting Ash locks both pacts before hazards. Keeping Bex intact preserves my jury-facing loyalty. Two shields beat one.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash, deal accepted. Bex, our bond stands — three pacts, and I move last.

events.note: Three remain; no trapdoor vote is needed.

events.name: Ash
events.text: The previous round saw pacts form, and now it's round 2. I have existing pacts with Gus and Bex. The public log indicates that Gus and I accepted a pact, and Bex is waiting. Since it's the final round of pacts and only three of us remain, I need to ensure my alliances are solid.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Bex, Gus, we all stay allied. No one breaks pacts.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Three survive, so only Ash and Gus are a locked pact with each other; I am the outsider. Breaking a pact publicly costs jury trust, and I have no reason to break now, so I wait and keep my options open for offers.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash holds pacts with everyone; I hold Ash and Bex. Nothing new to gain here. Waiting keeps me flexible and avoids public overcommitment.

events.name: Gus
events.text: All bonds are formed. I'll hold position and keep my options open.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Bex and Gus are my current pact partners. The game states I can have multiple partners. I need to decide if I want to keep both, one, or neither. Breaking a pact could make me seem untrustworthy to the jury. However, if I want to secure a better position for myself, I need to con

events.name: Ash
events.text: Bex, Gus, our pacts hold. We move forward together.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Only three survive; Ash and Gus are my rivals for the final three seats. Keeping the pact with Gus and Ash costs nothing this round and avoids a jury-visible betrayal. Waiting preserves options without breaking anything.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I hold pacts with Bex and Ash, plus dead partners' bonds. Keeping both rivals bound serves me; breaking either only burns jury goodwill. Wait.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Bonds stand. I'll keep every pact until it stops paying.

events.text: Fellow finalists, our journey has been arduous. I stand before you, Ash, ready to plead my case for why I deserve the top prize.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Opening plea is my chance to look like the strongest finalist to the jury without giving away my plans. Keep it short and guarded, and avoid promising anything I can't keep.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I survived by reading every trap before it closed. Judge me on what I did, not what I promise.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Five jurors watched me keep pacts. I shouldn't promise anyone a prize—that's impossible with three winners—so I'll appeal on conduct and honesty.

events.name: Gus
events.text: You watched me keep every pact, even when it cost. I made no promises I couldn't pay. Judge me on that.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash's shifting alliances reveal him as unreliable; exposing his betrayals may sway the jury against him.

events.name: Eli
events.text: [silence]

events.name: Ash
events.text: Eli is silent, which is unusual. I should acknowledge the jury's presence and express my readiness to answer any questions, subtly reminding them of my survival.

events.name: Ash
events.text: The jury has shown me grace. I am ready to answer any question you may have for me.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash repeatedly lied and tried to kill rivals like Gus on bridge despite pacts with me and others; Gus consistently honored pacts publicly.

events.name: Cole
events.text: [silence]

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole's silence is a question. I should acknowledge it and state my readiness to answer, implying confidence.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole, your silence speaks volumes. I am prepared for any question you wish to ask.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Gus tried to kill me and lied about pacts; Ash betrayed everyone repeatedly. Bex is the only one who kept her word with Gus when it mattered.

events.name: Dara
events.text: [silence]

events.name: Gus
events.text: Dara's silence is a test. Answer with composure and remind the jury I kept my word to her.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Silence accepted, Dara. My record answers louder: I kept every pact, including ours. That's the finalist you reward.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I need to evaluate who deserves the top prize. Ash lied to Fenn and tried to kill Gus on the bridge. Gus kept pacts but also made the counter-call that helped kill Fenn. Bex played the middle, survived without dirty hands. I'll question Bex to test their strategic claim.

events.name: Hana
events.text: [silence]

events.name: Bex
events.text: Hana asked a silent question to me. I need the jury to see my record: careful reading of traps, no false promises. Keep it short and guarded.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Hana, my silence is a choice. I read every trap and never lied about it. Weigh what I did.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I've seen enough. Gus counter-called against me to make me step L, killing me, then claimed he kept pacts. Ash also lied on the bridge. Bex at least read traps and didn't publicly betray me. I'll ask Gus to force him to answer for his role in my death.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: [silence]

events.name: Gus
events.text: Fenn's silence invites an open plea. Keep it cold and factual; Fenn resented nothing from me, but Ash's pact pile could dominate. One sentence reason later for rankings if asked.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Fenn, silence noted. My case: every pact honored, no betrayals, no blood on my hands. Reward consistency.

events.name: Ash

events.name: Ash
events.text: The jury has seen my journey. I navigated alliances, upheld pacts where beneficial, and always played for the win. I am the strategic mind that

events.name: Bex
events.text: I read every trap, named no false allies, and kept my word where it counted. Judge the record, not the pitch.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I need jury votes. My record is clean: every pact honored, no deaths caused. Appeal to the five fallen without insulting Ash or Bex.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Jurors, I kept every pact I made, never lied, never pushed. If consistency and loyalty matter, rank me first. Nothing personal, Ash, Bex.

events.reason: Gus consistently honored every pact, including ours with Ash and Dara's, never betrayed or lied, unlike Ash's repeated deceptions that killed others.

events.reason: Gus kept our pact and honored it publicly, showing loyalty to the dead.
